# Meet: Your own study

## Prepare the count matrix and metadata

Place inputs in `data/my-study/`:

| File | Required layout |
|---|---|
| `gene-counts.tsv` | First column `gene_id`; one unique gene per row; one raw integer-count column per sample |
| `sample-metadata.tsv` | First column `sample_id`; one unique row per sample; supported design columns |

Use tab-separated text with exact matching sample IDs. Do not supply TPM, FPKM, CPM, log counts or transformed expression to this matrix interface. Rounding normalized values does not recover raw counts. Quantification workflows requiring transcript-level imports need a suitable documented adaptation.

## Match the script's actual design interface

| Metadata layout | Model used | Contrast |
|---|---|---|
| `group` containing A and B, no `donor` | `~ group` | B relative to A |
| `group` A/B plus `donor`, one sample per donor in each group | `~ donor + group` | B relative to A, accounting for donor |
| `cell` plus `dex` containing untrt/trt, one of each per cell line | `~ cell + dex` | trt relative to untrt, accounting for cell line |

If both `cell` and `dex` exist, the script chooses that layout before checking `group`. Do not leave misleading unused airway-style columns in your input. Other covariates are not automatically added to the design.

Keep condition/source encodings and their original meanings documented. Unsupported designs require an explicit code change and review, not fabricated pairing or condition labels.

## Preserve provenance

Record source, organism, count-generation method, annotation version, date and any identifier changes. Resolve duplicated gene labels using a documented upstream rule rather than dropping rows arbitrarily. Do not treat technical runs as independent biological replicates.

The current checker rejects missing values anywhere in metadata. Keep the supplied table focused on complete, required analysis variables; preserve fuller source metadata separately. Never fill an unknown donor or condition with an invented value merely to pass checks.

**Your task:** trace one sample across matrix and metadata, identify its biological source and explain the selected design row. Protect participant identifiers before sharing files or AI prompts.
